testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of a vehicle's air brake system?
questions.explanation: An air brake system includes an air compressor, governor, storage tanks, drains, alcohol evaporator, safety valve, brake pedal, foundation brakes, pressure gauges, warning signals, stop light switch, brake limiting valve, spring brakes, and parking brake controls. An air filter is not part of this system.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: A yellow light means:
questions.explanation: Vehicles with anti-lock brakes have a yellow light. This light comes on when there is a problem with the braking system.

questions.question: What should happen before air pressure in an air brake tank drops below 55 psi?

options.text: The vehicle will be unable to shift out of gear.

questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light must come on before air pressure drops below 55 psi. If this light does not work during inspection, the vehicle is unsafe to drive.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, the parking brake is applied by:

options.text: Moving a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull it out to apply the brakes. Push it in to release the brakes.

questions.question: Not draining air tanks can cause:

options.text: Water accumulations freezing and causing brake failure.
Too much air collecting in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water accumulations freezing and causing brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve sits between the air compressor and main reservoir. It prevents air from escaping the system if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: An application pressure gauge shows:

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is required to stop a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. This helps drivers spot brake fade early.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Are helpful to remove water and oil from the air tanks.
Are used to move air to the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are helpful to remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and oil. These can damage the system if they build up. Drain valves remove water and oil from the tanks.

questions.question: Brakes can quickly go out of adjustment, especially when:
questions.explanation: Hot brakes go out of adjustment quickly. Check your brake adjustment regularly. All brakes must be in good working order for safe vehicle control.

questions.question: What causes friction in an S-cam brake?

options.text: Brake shoes and linings press against the outside of the brake drum.
Brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the brake drum.
Brake shoes and linings push against each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction happens when brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the brake drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.explanation: Air brake vehicles must have a low pressure warning device. A wig wag drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi.

questions.question: What should you do with the parking brake when leaving your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Only use it if the vehicle is parked on a slope.
Do not use it because it damages the tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when leaving your vehicle. Do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and temperatures are below freezing.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice buildup in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: What does the S-cam do when it turns inside a brake drum?

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Presses the brake shoes against the brake linings.
Presses the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: What can happen if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too much lets air out faster than the compressor can replace it. Air brakes may stop working if pressure gets too low.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: Know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle type. A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: What allows a driver to gradually apply spring brakes?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver gradually apply spring brakes. A lever on the dashboard controls this valve.

questions.question: If you use spring brakes while hauling a heavy load, how long will it take to stop?

options.text: It will be impossible to stop.
It will take a long time.
It will take a short time.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will take a long time.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. If they activate due to low air pressure, your vehicle needs a longer distance to stop, especially with a heavy load.

questions.question: What should a driver do when leaving a vehicle unattended?

options.text: Only set the parking brake if parked on a slope.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: Do not drive a vehicle if any brake drum has a crack larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums before each trip during your walk-around inspection. It is unsafe to drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: If an air compressor uses a belt to run, the belt should be regularly checked to make sure it is:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has air brakes, check the air compressor drive belt before each trip. Make sure the belt is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: What is commonly found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: How many feet does an air brake-equipped vehicle need to stop from 55 mph in ideal driving conditions?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake-equipped vehicle traveling at 55 mph needs about 450 feet to stop completely under ideal conditions.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended:

options.text: You must always use the parking brake.
You should never use the parking brake.
You should lower the cab windows.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always use the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.
